I let the verb love conjugate all subjects
My sentences begin in the middle and never end
I put adjectives of color on nouns of sadness

title: The Dialogue of the Rain and the Window
poemText: The rain said to the window
Why are you so cold and so hard
Why are you so sad and so wet
I weep for the sorrow of the world
I would like to pass through you to comfort the people
Me, I would like to break to let them out
That the window shattered into a thousand pieces
And the rain entered the house
And the people went out into the street
They danced together in the rain

title: The Clocks' Strike
poemText: One Tuesday morning at exactly eight o'clock
All the clocks in the town stopped
The one at the station the one at the church the one at the post office
The wristwatches the alarm clocks the Swiss cuckoo clocks
They had had enough of slicing life into pieces
Enough of running after a future that never arrives
Enough of eating seconds like dry insects
People went out into the streets
They looked at each other for the first time
They had a coffee that lasted for hours
It was the most beautiful day in the world
For no one ever knew what time it was to end it.

poemText: At midnight when the city sleeps
Shadows detach themselves from the walls
And meet in the Place de la République
The banker's shadow is long and thin
The worker's shadow is bent by fatigue
The lover's shadow seeks the shadow of their love
They exchange their shapes their secrets their regrets
The dog's shadow pees on the general's shadow
Just the grand democracy of the night
Then the first ray of sun arrives
To cling to the feet of its owner

title: Blue, the Color of Dreams
poemText: I am not a color that screams
I am a great murmur, a sigh
The color of that which is far away
The horizon, the sea, and the vein on a hand
I am the color of escape
The immense sky that belongs to no one
And where the birds draw poems of freedom
I am the deep ocean full of voyages and monsters
The liquid road to unknown islands
I am the uniform of the sailor who is leaving
And the color of the eyes in which one drowns in love
I am the color of dreams and of hope
The blue smoke of a wood fire rising to the stars
The ink of the letter one is waiting for
And the little flame of the gas in the silent night
But I am also the color of sorrow
The "blues" of the black musician in a Chicago bar
The color of lips when one is cold
The terrible blue of a bruise on the skin and on the soul
I am the color of the work uniform
The "bleu de travail" that smells of sweat and fatigue
The faded blue of a life spent in a factory
Looking at the sky through a dirty window
I am the greatest of paradoxes
The color of the cage and of freedom
I am the blue of the worker's overalls
And the blue of the sky he looks at while dreaming
I am the distance between what one is
And what one would like to be
I am the color of the human soul
A great sea of desires and of melancholy.

title: Yellow, the Color of Laughter
poemText: I am the color of laughter and of the sun

The liquid heart of a fried egg

The color of sickness on a man's skin
The yellow and feverish light of a tired lightbulb
The pages of an old book that are slowly dying

The one that is neither yes nor no

And the fake gold of a cheap ring
That leaves a green trace on the finger
I am joy, but a joy that knows it does not last
The beauty of summer just before autumn
A laughter that is on the verge of tears
I am the most cheerful and the most unsettling of colors
Before the shadow comes to take it all back.

title: The Swifts

the façade the gutters the plaster

title: The Silence in the Library
poemText: On the library door hangs a sign
and the woman at the desk puts a finger to her lips
as in a room where someone is sleeping
it is the loudest place in town
louder than the square on market day
only it is heard with the eyes
here a thousand voices speak at once
poets dead a hundred years speak
and complain and laugh and cry out
you open a book and the talking begins
here is the storm here is the war
here someone whispers I love you
here a ship goes down and no one hears
except you with your finger on the line
the woman at the desk knows it best
that is why she makes this silence
not so that people should be quiet
but so that those may be heard
who can no longer speak any other way
she wants everyone to be able to speak
the dead and the living all at once
and that is only possible in silence
and so the library is full of uproar
full of singing and weeping and laughter
under the sign that says SILENCE PLEASE
and silence is not the ban on speaking
so that at last everyone can

title: The Taxi Driver Who Turns Off the Meter
poemText: The taxi waits at the station rank
the driver reaches out his hand

when the man beside him clutches a little suitcase

just a field and one pear tree

going to the first funeral of his life

the one to the pear tree in fifty years going back

title: The Summer Cinema Projectionist
poemText: The open-air cinema behind the brewery
a screen stretched between two poplars
three hundred chairs under the stars
at the back the projection booth
and in the booth the projectionist

says the ticket lady closing her window
the beam flies over the empty chairs
and in the beam dance the moths and the dust
the most faithful audience in the world

lovers soldiers horses and the sea
a film that is never shown
would you let the sea die?

the ticket lady sells a single ticket
and sits in the middle of three hundred chairs

the actress's trunk that weighs more than the actress

title: The Magpie and the Wedding Ring
poemText: She left it on the ledge by the sink
just while she did the dishes
with a date and a name engraved inside
and a shine is a shine
and all that was left of the ring
was a wet little circle on the sill
thirty years I never took it off
and in the morning he borrowed a ladder
Up in the poplar in the nest
and in the middle of it all
and left the foil where it was
so she would have something too
Down in the kitchen he went down
on one knee that creaked by now
and slid the ring on her finger a second time
except both their hands were shaking

title: The Staircase without a Lift
poemText: House number twelve has no lift
and on every floor two lives
On the ground floor the lady who bakes
her scent rises free of charge
all the way to the fourth
on the first the man with the cello

they take the stairs two at a time going up
three at a time coming down
once they carried a pram up
and since then they count the steps too
the steps outside it are the quietest

half an hour to the top
at the baking lady's floor he breathes in
at the young couple's he smiles
at the empty flat he takes off his hat

and on the way I meet the whole house
the scent the music the children the silence

the step where I start taking off my shoes

that over four floors is learning

title: The Fresco Restorer
poemText: High on the scaffolding under the vault
the pious overpainting of zealous repairs
a sky four hundred years old
And then at the edge of a cloud
where no one can see from the nave
she finds a fingerprint in the plaster
the painter leaned on the fresh wall
maybe his wife was laughing down below
The committee asks from the floor
have you found anything of value
She sets her finger beside the print
the way you shake a hand
she says later for the report
but the most alive thing of all
is the touch of a tired man

title: The Street Portraitist
poemText: On the bridge sits the portraitist
a sign propped against his suitcase
says a student with a sketchbook under his arm
that's not what they look like
The portraitist doesn't put down his charcoal
the way their dog sees them
the way their mother saw them
the second before the bathroom light comes on
One day an old lady comes
sits up straight as in school
And he draws for a long time
the way you read a letter
The old lady looks at the paper
and says nothing for a long while
How much do I owe you
says the portraitist packing up his charcoals
the true ones I give away

title: The Cello on the Tram
poemText: At the theatre stop a cellist gets on
and with him a big black case
he settles it carefully on a seat
The inspector works his way down the aisle
The cellist hands over two tickets
This gentleman was born in seventeen ninety
first the lady with her shopping
who gives the case a salute
asks a little girl across the aisle
it grew a hundred years in the mountains
and then it learned to sing
now it rides the number nine
the tram rattles over the bridge
which won't play a single note the whole way
At the terminus the cellist gets off last
the driver tells him in the mirror

title: The Proofreader
poemText: forty years of other people's mistakes
sentences that set out and never arrived
words split in the worst possible place
She has corrected novels and train timetables
and not one of them was hers
on the last page it says
But the wife has been dead thirty years
it says so in the very first chapter
The proofreader raises her red pencil
The pencil hangs a moment over the paper
like a wasp over a glass
And then the proofreader erases her mark
the only one in forty years
the past tense and the present tense
the tense of those who are gone
and read over your shoulder anyway
and some are left to live

the Vasek girl out of the pond last year

every wrong note comes from the heart

title: The Lullaby Singer
poemText: Every evening she sings to the children
the most grateful audience in the world
in the middle of the second verse
and the children breathe more slowly
a small hand lets go of the plush dog
even the long note at the end
Who do you sing the ending for
her husband asks one night from the doorway
she says switching off the lamp
For the dark so it knows
we lend it the child for one night only
for the room so it remembers the tune
in case the child should wake
she says already in the hallway
who always used to fall asleep
in the middle of the second verse
and all her life has wanted to know
The beginnings of songs are for children
and still want to hear every night

title: The Last Night Flight
poemText: The airport at one in the morning
the departure board has played its last hand
the perfume shop sleeps behind its grille
the coffee machine keeps its light on
The cleaning woman rides her machine
across a hall as big as a town square
even the sniffer dog is asleep
Only the tower is still lit
and across the screen a dot is traveling
And the controller watches the dot
and wonders who is sitting in it
maybe a woman flying to a funeral
rehearsing her first sentence in silence
maybe a man coming home after twenty years
afraid he's forgotten the name of his street
maybe a child flying for the first time
asleep with its forehead on the window
above a land full of small lights
And for that one little dot
the whole airport lights up again
the runway the hall the belts
and the sign ARRIVALS above the doors
because no one is allowed to land in the dark
and no one in this world

title: The Hitchhiker with a Sign Saying Anywhere
poemText: At the edge of the road past the last house
holding a sign made from a banana box
and on it in big letters
That's not a direction young man
It's the best direction in the world
the only one you can't miss
I'm only going as far as Slough
but the driver is already rolling up his window
Slough suddenly seems very small to him
A second car stops a third a fifth
and they all ask the same thing
and the hitchhiker lifts his sign a little higher
I'm only going to my mother-in-law's
and each one in his rearview mirror
carries away a piece of that word
Toward evening an old car pulls over
Where are you going? asks the hitchhiker
I've been driving since morning that's all
Then that makes two of us
says the hitchhiker and gets in
And the sign lies on the back seat
and for the first time all day
it points exactly the right way

title: The Road that Led Nowhere
poemText: Past the village a road begins
with an avenue of old cherry trees
and a little bridge over the brook
It starts out grandly like all roads do
in the middle of the oats
like a sentence someone never finished
Once they say it was meant to reach a town
or a bridge that changed its mind
the plans went yellow in the district archive
The authorities twice tried to strike it off
a road without a destination shall be cancelled
it says so in the regulations
but there was never money for that
and so it keeps on leading
lovers because they meet no one there
an old man with a cane because he has nowhere to get to
a lady with a dog that chases wind through the oats
children on bikes riding to the end of the world
and home in time for supper
Every other road drives you somewhere
to work to the office to the train
only this one is in no hurry at all
and that is why it walks so well
And at the very end in the oats
from all the people standing there looking

title: The Boundary Stone
poemText: On the bank between Upper End and Lower End
a stone sits in the grass
a U carved on one side
an L carved on the other
Once upon a time it was serious
the mayors took the meadow to court
the farmers brawled at the parish fair
sealed documents sleep in the archive
that the line runs exactly here
it grows across the line in both directions
the swallows fly from one land register to the other
the rain rains on both villages at once
the hare has its burrow right on the border
head in Upper End rump in Lower End
the Upper End cow grazes Lower End grass
and in the evening she gives milk
and that milk is one milk only
Only people know where the line is
children know it best of all
they sit on the stone with their sandwiches
because whoever sits on the stone
is neither in Upper End nor in Lower End
that is the best seat there is

title: The Highway Diner
poemText: The waitress brings coffee and the soup of the day

what people elsewhere won't tell in a lifetime

the woman by the window is driving away from someone
you can tell by how long
she stirs a coffee with no sugar in it
so as not to hear himself for a while
and the soldier on leave says nothing

because they will never see her again

title: The Last Stop of the Cable Car
poemText: The cable car climbs out of the valley
over the spruces over the clearing
a tin shed a great wheel
and a sign saying END OF THE LINE
beyond there is nothing at all
and the wind that has lived here forever
An old man with a thermos runs the station
he greets the cabins like old acquaintances
and all day long he answers
The tourists take pictures by the sign
eat their sandwiches on the sheltered side of the shed
But now and then somebody stays standing
looking at the ridge above the station
You can't ride up there says the old man
up there you can only walk
higher still you can only look
Everything in this world stretches only as far as it will
he says screwing his thermos shut
they always stop a little short of the summit
the last stretch everyone must climb alone
it can only be stood in silence

what has once been written must arrive

title: Radio for the Sleepless
poemText: At two in the morning a voice speaks on the radio

the watchman listens not yet in bed
the mother with a child on her shoulder
the truck driver between two towns
the old man whose bed is too big
and the boy afraid to switch off the light

and the voice on the radio speaks
as if sitting in each of their rooms

in twenty years nobody has written to me
so I'll ask you just one thing
turn your light on for a moment

here and there and over there too
by the station on the ground floor under the tower
a whole constellation of the sleepless

and for the first time in twenty years
he isn't saying it to the dark

the one Mr Josef once saved
the only one of his life

title: The Second Hand
poemText: On the clock there are three hands
The hour hand is the director
in a whole day it hardly moves
and yet the world sets itself by it
The minute hand is the office clerk
once an hour it walks around the office
and goes back to standing still
And then there is the third one
the only one you can see running
It runs all day all night
three thousand six hundred an hour
And when someone asks the time
the way the errand boy is cropped
When the doctor holds a sick man's wrist
he doesn't look at the director

title: Monday
poemText: On Sunday evening around eleven o'clock Monday already arrives in the suburbs of the week It makes no noise It waits on the doormat of time With its gray briefcase full of duties And its rain-colored coat

At dawn it enters the city without knocking It is a zealous civil servant First it repaints the sky With a thick coat of administrative gray Then it turns off the last lingering dreams And it turns on the alarm clocks All at the same time A siren's cry to announce the end of recess

Monday walks in the streets And everything stands at attention It steals the taste from the coffee It puts sand in the eyes of children It replaces kisses with handshakes It teaches people to walk in a straight line With heads bowed and shoulders slumped It checks that the clocks are on time On the time of sadness and efficiency

Under its reign the city is a large waiting room One waits for lunch One waits for the end of the day One waits for Friday Laughter is forbidden before nine in the morning Sighs are tolerated but not encouraged Even the birds sing a little less loudly As if they were afraid to disturb

But Monday is not all-powerful Look closely In the metro a young girl is reading a poem A small act of colorful disobedience On the fogged-up window of a bus A child's finger has drawn a mocking sun A man and a woman send each other a message Just one word "courage" A small lifebuoy in the ocean of the day

In the evening Monday is tired Its work is done It packs up its gray and its obligations It leaves again on tiptoe Leaving behind an exhausted city But where in the black sky The first star lights up Like a stubborn promise That all is not yet lost.

title: Jupiter, the Stormy King
poemText: After the red soldier and his silence of rust
I am the king, the giant, the big gentleman
I am not made of earth nor of regrets
I am made of gas, of anger, and of solitude
I have no ground to place my feet on
My only land is my own immense weight
I am a painter who paints only with storms
My colors are ocher, brick, and old gold
My brushes are winds of a thousand kilometers per hour
I paint ribbons of clouds that never dry
And in the middle of it all, I have my masterpiece
A cyclone's eye open for centuries
That stares into the void without ever blinking
It is the signature of my melancholy
I have a large family of little moons
My court of silent and faithful servants
They dance around me to try to calm me
They polish my great ball of gas with their little light
That you cannot calm a storm
I am the big protective brother of the family
The goalkeeper of the solar system
With my immense body, I catch the stray stones
The drunken comets that would like to do harm
To my fragile little sisters, Earth or Venus
It is a thankless and solitary job
They are too busy with their little lives
To see the dangers I divert for them
So I turn heavily in the dark
The beating heart of the great celestial clockwork
A king without a castle, a god without prayers
A father who protects his children from afar
And who can only show them
I am the great storm that will never end.

title: Mars, the Old Soldier
poemText: After my sister Earth, noisy and full of life,
I am the fourth, the tired soldier
They call me the God of War
A ridiculous old name for an old man like me
My great wars have been over for millions of years
My armor is covered in rust
And that rust is my only color
I remember a time when I was blue
A time when I wore rivers on my face
Tears of clear water that flowed in my great canyons
Perhaps I remember the taste of rain
And the murmur of a wind that was not made of dust
That was before the great drought
Today my kingdom is a red desert
My mountains are volcanoes asleep forever
My army is a storm of fine sand
That marches with no purpose and no enemy
My only treasures are two small pieces of ice
At my poles like two cold medals
I am the king of an immense silence
The guardian of a dead world
Little metal insects that my sister Earth sends
They roll slowly over my skin
They take pictures of my old scars
They search for signs of life with their little glass eyes
Like children searching for treasure in an empty attic
I am too old for anger
Their curiosity is a small, touching thing
I look at them and I look at my sister in the distance
That blue and white marble so full of noise and fury
How lucky she is to have water to cry with
I have nothing left but red dust
So I wrap myself in my thin, cold atmosphere
Like in an old military blanket

title: Mercury, the Hurried Messenger
poemText: I am the first the closest
The little messenger of the great king Sun
I run I run I never stop
My race is my prayer and my madness
But I have no mouth to speak it
And there is no one to hear it
I have two faces like a liar or a lover
Burned with love and with light
A land of molten rock and of despair
Where silence boils under a sky of fire
It is the face of the eternal "yes"
My other face is turned toward the void
Frozen by solitude and by night
A plain of black ice and absolute silence
Where the stars are cold pinpricks
And I live ceaselessly between these two extremes
Between the kiss that burns and the absence that freezes
The other planets watch me from afar
They turn slowly in their queenly gowns
They see me as a little fool a nervous spark
They do not understand my haste and my devotion
They do not know what it is
To love a fire that devours you
On my skin I have scars
The memories of an old war of pebbles
Each crater is a letter of an unknown alphabet
That tells the story of my terrible birth
My message is written on my face
But no one knows how to read it
With one side of my body on fire
The first word in the great king's sentence
The first servant and the first prisoner
I am the spinning top that the Sun has launched
And that will never stop turning.

The blue of the great void

The god of an ocean that no longer remembers water
And I listen to the song of my furious winds
The only proof that I am not

title: Saturn, the Sad Ballerina
poemText: And his great uproar of storms
I am the queen of silence
I am not heavy I am light
They say I could float on the ocean
I only dream of stopping floating
Around my waist I have my adornment and my prison
My beautiful rings of ice and dust
The other planets look at them with envy
They do not know what it is
To eternally wear the debris of a broken love
The frozen memory of a lost moon
I am a sad ballerina in a giant music box
I turn slowly on my axis
My dress is a hoop of diamonds and frost
A silent carousel for the ghosts of light
A great necklace of frozen tears
My little moons are my only spectators
They watch me turn with faithful eyes
On the other side of my beautiful barrier of ice
I am the most beautiful perhaps
Beauty is a cold thing that creates distance
I do not have the anger of Mars nor the life of Earth
I do not have the fire of the Sun nor the poison of Venus
I have only my cold and perfect beauty
I am the great white sigh of the solar system
The forgotten pearl at the bottom of the night's jewelry box
Who has decorated the walls of his cell.

title: Uranus, the Silent Rebel
poemText: After the sad dance of Saturn
I am the seventh, the strange one, the eccentric
All the other planets stand up straight
Like well-behaved soldiers or obedient spinning tops
I have lain down on my side
It was not an accident, a cosmic shoving match
I had had enough of looking up and down
I wanted to look at the world from the side
To see if the universe was different from that point of view
It is my small, silent revolution
My act of laziness and of disobedience
I do not spin, I roll
Like a child in the grass or a barrel of blue wine
My kingdom is of a pale and quiet color
A blue-green of a frozen lagoon
I do not have the great angers of Jupiter
Nor the ostentatious jewels of Saturn
My beauty is discreet and uneventful
I am a great calm eye floating in the dark
My few rings are so thin
They look like forgotten spider threads
And my moons have names from poetry
They are characters from old, sad plays
My only companions in the great cold
From afar they look at me with curiosity
The tilted planet, the anomaly of the system
They wonder if I am sick or tired
They do not understand that rest can be a form of protest
That silence can be a strong word
So I continue my long and slow roll
In the distant suburbs of the Sun's kingdom
I am at peace with my own strangeness
That there is more than one way to dance
Around the great fire of life.

title: Venus, the Veiled Beauty
poemText: The shepherd's star, the evening star
The lovers on Earth look at me and sigh
They give me the name of their most beautiful goddess
They see only my great cloak of clouds
My gown of white and golden silk
They do not see what lies beneath
If a poet came here seeking love
He would find an oven, a hell
My air is not air, it is a poison that crushes
My rain is not water, it is acid that burns
My kisses are bites of fire
I am the great queen of solitude
My kingdom is a desert of red rocks
Where volcanoes shout their stony anger
There is not a single bird, not a single flower
The silence here is not the silence of peace
It is the heavy silence of death
Nothing can live beneath my beautiful poisoned gown
They call me Earth's twin sister
When it locks itself in its own heat
So I turn slowly on my axis
In my magnificent prison of gas
I am the brightest in the night sky
And no one sees my sorrow
I am the promise of an impossible beauty
The love that one can only admire from very, very far away.

The blue marble in the great silent game
I am not made of fire nor of poison

I carry on my back oceans that dream
And mountains that scratch the belly of the clouds
Those that crawl, those that swim, those that fly
And then I have my strangest children
They have a mad talent for beauty
They know how to make a stone or a piece of wood speak
They write poems that make me weep with joy
They invent music that makes the stars dance
They know the taste of warm bread
The warmth of a friendly hand
And the sweetness of a kiss in the rain
But they also have a mad talent for foolishness
They draw lines on my skin and call them borders
They wage war over pieces of land that belong to me
They build factories that make me cough up black smoke
They cover my meadows with cement and sadness
They speak of love and they make bombs

The only inhabited house on the street of the sun
The only planet with laughter and wars
My distant sisters are clean and tidy
They are perfect in their hell or their solitude
I am messy, I am full of scars
I am noisy and dirty and magnificent and sick
I am their mother, their home, their ship
I wait for them to grow up a little
I wait for them to understand
That the only border that matters
Is the one between tenderness and cruelty.

title: The Sun, the Lonely King

I shout in the ear of the roosters
And I paint a fine line of gold under the door of the sleepers
I am the great painter without a brush
Without me the flower is a gray shape
The ocean a large black spot
The face of the beloved a simple absence
I give the red to the cherry
And the changing blue of the eyes that look at the sky

I am the great clothes dryer of the world
Who dries the shirts of workers and the dresses of lovers

Like a worker going home after a long day

Who comes to console the world from my great light

title: June, the Lazy King
poemText: After May the queen has exhausted all her perfumes
He is not a decorator nor a revolutionary
He is a lazy king who inherits a perfect kingdom
He sees that the work is already done
The trees are green the flowers are open
So he lies down in the tall grass
And begins his long reign of heat and light
His first royal decree is for the sun
He orders it to climb very high and to stop moving
Except for a little breeze to make the leaves shiver
So that naps in the shade can last an eternity
The green of the leaves darkens and gorges on sap
The blue of the sky becomes intense and cloudless
He paints the cheeks of the first cherries
He sprinkles the fields with the red dots of poppies
And the blue dots of cornflowers
The city also slows its mad race
The asphalt is soft and hot
People seek the shade of the plane trees
They drink cool drinks on café terraces
The only sound is the buzzing of insects
And the distant laughter of children playing with water
The nights are short and warm
Nights of blue velvet where one can sleep with the window open
Listening to the scent of jasmine
June is the guardian of the longest day of the year
The summit of the great mountain of light
A suspended moment where everything is accomplished
Where everything is ripe and heavy with kept promises
There is nothing to do but to be
To breathe the warm air to feel the sun on one's skin
The lazy king does not worry
He knows that the light will now begin to decline
He has offered the world a moment of motionless perfection
And the memory of a summer that was just beginning.

poemText: on page one thousand two hundred forty
Once it was in every kitchen
and it stayed only in crosswords
The dictionary kept it out of mercy
at every revision there was a vote
strike it, keep it, strike it
in a village near the border
Her grandson sat by the bed
and read to her from old books
from page one thousand two hundred forty
for the first time in three days
and with that word came back
the lamp, the table, the smell
And the word returned to its page
and no longer fears being struck
open at least one pair of eyes

title: The Last Page of the Calendar

under the weight of all the others

a hand will tear it off

the March ones in a hurry
the holiday ones with sand in their dates
the November ones no one mourned

a page with the same date
into every one of my brothers

title: The Compass
poemText: that's my obsession and my service
and to all of them I said the same:
a compass doesn't know the destination
a compass knows only one fixed direction
and from it all the others can be derived
because that's the whole trick of orientation:
you don't need to know where the destination is
you need to know one sure direction
A mountaineer kept me in his pocket
when night caught him in the fog
and I didn't tell him the way down
that the hut lay north to south
and down in the warmth he said:
that little thing didn't lead me home
that little thing only told me
I'd just forgotten it in the panic
and that's the whole wisdom of the compass:
from which the rest is reckoned
and you'll never be entirely lost
